sources.title: GitLab Threat Intelligence Team reveals North Korean tradecraft

disclaimer: Kim Won Jin (김원진; Won-Jin Kim in the report) is profiled here as a member of the North Korean IT-worker cell that GitLab Threat Intelligence assesses is managed by Kang Kil Nam and is highly likely colocated and operating from Beijing. GitLab's assessed organization chart places Kim Won Jin as a cell member in Working Group Two. GitLab reports that in the third quarter of 2025 Kim Won Jin was dropped from tracking and the related documentation was moved to a directory marked 귀국 ("return to the home country"), and assesses that the departure is unlikely to relate to earnings, which had been consistently high relative to other members.
The report gives this name in romanised form only. The Hangul above is this site's reconstruction from that romanisation and is not cited; search the romanised name.

GitLab reports that the cell's personnel dossiers describe every member as a researcher at the Kim Il-sung University Joint Research Center in Beijing (베이징주재 김일성종합대학 공동연구중심 연구사), and suggests the cell's presence in China may be under an academic pretext.

The confidence level of 'medium' reflects that the name comes from GitLab's assessed organization chart and the cell's internal records as GitLab reads them. It is a private company's assessment, not a criminal charge, a sanctions designation or a court finding.
